name: SAIF-driven gate-level dynamic power measurement
flow: synth DCP (OOC) -> write_verilog -mode funcsim netlist (preserves RTL net names)
iverilog gate-level sim (unisims + bram stubs + glbl) -> gl.vcd
vcd_to_saif.py (strip tb scopes, dcp-name filter, bus bit-expansion) -> gl_power.saif
Vivado read_saif + report_power on OOC DCP

simulation.engine: Icarus Verilog (xsim BASIC license caps at 50k instances; DUT=211k)

prior_e13_xpower.note: RTL-sim VCD failed to match P&R net names (0/398749); default-activity only

delta.note: SAIF vs default-activity on same OOC DCP

key_findings: 99% net annotation resolves E13's 0% match failure; confidence Medium -> High
BRAM is 89.7% of dynamic power (0.331/0.369 W): design is memory-bound, BRAM clock gating is the dominant power lever
Default 50% toggle assumption overestimates CLB logic power 43.6x (0.305 -> 0.007 W): NTT pipeline is memory-bound and most LUTs idle most cycles
Total SAIF power 0.824 W vs 1.182 W (E13 XPower) and 1.316 W (default activity on same DCP): prior numbers were conservative by 30-37%
Noise monitor (u_nmon) costs 0.003 W = 0.8% of dynamic: the closed-loop SNR feedback is nearly free in power
Key-switch unit u_ksw dominates dynamic (0.146 W, 39.6%) followed by shared poly-mult engine u_pm_shared (0.075 W, 20.3%)
caveats: Design is synthesized (OOC), not placed-and-routed: implementation-state confidence Low; post-route numbers may differ
OOC subtree power, not full-chip: device static 0.455 W is the xcau25p floor; no I/O, no PS, no board components
Activity from 2 encrypted-multiply window at 100 MHz on funcsim netlist (BRAM stubbed, not real BRAM behavior)
Relative comparisons (SAIF vs default on same DCP, vs E13 static estimate) are valid; absolute W should be quoted as synthesis-level estimate
